name: Tetanus antitoxin

overview.mechanism: Provides passive antitoxin against tetanus toxin.
uses: Tetanus antitoxin use must follow the exact equine product insert and clinical indication; it is distinct from human tetanus immunoglobulin and tetanus toxoid.

sources.citation: FDA Philippines product records preserved in website registry shards; exact generic heading inspected 2026-11-25. Cached identity information, not a new verification of present registration validity or product insert.

Nguyen Van Hao, et al. Human versus equine intramuscular antitoxin, with or without human intrathecal antitoxin, for the treatment of adults with tetanus: a 2×2 factorial randomised controlled trial. Lancet Glob Health.2022;10:e 862–e 872. PMID 35561721.

draft_notes: Exact Philippine product insert governs dosing. No preparation, species, route or dialysis regimen transferred from a different product.

Equine exact-product insert link was found in registry but not retrievable via web tool. Empty contraindications/interactions arrays intentionally avoid inventing or transferring human-TIG rules. This entry remains a descriptive monograph rather than a complete prescribing insert.

revision_log.change: New source-linked descriptive monograph, exact cached product identity separated from comparator US labeling or clinical research.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

usual_adult_dose.indication: Exact equine product and indication required
usual_adult_dose.dose: No regimen inferred from human TIG or trial doses. The cached equine products have differing IU/mL and vial contents; confirm the specific insert before calculating volume [[PHREG,TETRCT]]

serious: Equine antitoxin has historical allergic-reaction concerns; the selected adult trial did not show a clinically relevant between-group adverse-event difference. This does not exclude rare severe reactions [[TETRCT]]

monitoring: In the adult trial, adverse events were assessed alongside tetanus severity and need for mechanical ventilation; these research procedures do not replace product-specific hypersensitivity precautions [[TETRCT]]

evidence.title: Equine identity and treatment evidence
evidence.intro: Confirm the exact equine product insert for contraindications, hypersensitivity precautions and dosing. The trial below does not establish a renal or dialysis regimen.

rows.design: Six equine records: Sharjvax(BR-807/808/809/BRP-073), Tetadeel(BRP-073-01), tetAMSON(BRP-073-02).
rows.intervention: Presentations range from 1500 IU/0.7 mL to 10000 IU/10 mL; several records explicitly list IM.
rows.findings: These are equine antitoxin records, not human TIG. Milliliters must not be transferred between concentrations.
rows.limitations: Cached registry identity is not an approved dosing or contraindication section.

rows.design: Factorial randomized trial;272 adults overall;218 eligible for the randomized human/equine IM allocation.
rows.intervention: Human versus equine IM antitoxin for established adult tetanus, separately from intrathecal allocation.
rows.findings: Mechanical ventilation 45% human versus 44% equine(RR 1.01;95% CI 0.75–1.36;P=0.95). Related/possibly related adverse events 16% human versus 15% equine; no intervention-related deaths.
rows.limitations: Specific adult treatment setting; no prophylaxis, pediatric, brand-equivalence or dialysis regimen established. Nonsignificant comparison is not proof that all products have identical safety.
